summary: The public-main and candidate-4 -> evidence-rescue -> candidate-5 ancestry is exact, linear, first-parent, and merge-free. The canonical source checkout, assigned review worktree, and batch manifest all bind to candidate d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec, and both Git worktrees were clean on separate branches. No ref tip contains audit-lock.json; the historical v1 lock was explicitly renamed and superseded before any lane transition, all 140 v2 units remain pending, and no prebaseline lane path exists. Baseline promotion is nevertheless blocked: an exact-candidate temporary lifecycle proved that the lock creator accepts staged unrelated bytes and the full post-lock validator accepts those bytes in the direct-child lock commit. PROJECT_STATUS.md also retains a contradictory dirty/pending-candidate-5 statement after candidate 5 is committed and clean.

findings.title: The direct-child lock commit may silently include unreviewed unrelated content
findings.claim: create_correctness_audit_lock.py binds baseline to HEAD and checks required locked-file/progress bytes, but it never requires a clean worktree/index. The post-lock validator proves that audit-lock.json is introduced in the baseline's first direct child, but it never constrains the other paths changed by that same commit. A staged unrelated tracked modification can therefore be swept into the authoritative lock commit after the reviewed baseline, and the complete post-lock validator still reports success.

evidence.detail: The creator rejects only an existing current-worktree audit-lock.json and then selects git rev-parse HEAD as baseline; there is no git status/index cleanliness check.
The creator compares the canonical locked-file set and progress bytes with the baseline, then writes audit-lock.json. It does not reject other dirty or staged paths.
The seal validator proves direct-child ancestry and exact lock-path bytes, and validate_lock guards locked paths, but neither checks the lock commit's complete changed-path set.

evidence.observed: After source staging, readme.md was modified but not staged. git status reported readme.md as .M; create_correctness_audit_lock.py exited 0 and emitted a stage1-v2 lock bound to d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec with 85 locked files.

evidence.probe: ephemeral exact-candidate lock-commit scope and post-lock lifecycle probe
evidence.observed: readme.md was modified and staged before creator execution. The creator exited 0. A normal commit after adding audit-lock.json produced direct child f6e785b1e5a84d5649c7ac89d90230235b304d43 with parent d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec and exactly two changed paths: A audit-lock.json and M readme.md. The complete uv-isolated post-lock validator exited 0 with passed=true, failureCount=0, failures=[]. The temporary clone was removed.

reproduction.preconditions: Clone exact candidate d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec, stage the 1,098 gitignored source files from /home/smithers/nemesis-retaliation, and configure a temporary Git identity.
steps: Modify readme.md and git add readme.md.
git add docs/qa/implementation-readiness/correctness-audit/audit-lock.json and run an ordinary git commit without a path restriction.
Verify the direct-child commit changes audit-lock.json and readme.md.
Run the pinned full post-lock validator; observe exit 0 and failureCount 0.
reproduction.expected: Lock creation must fail when any pre-existing tracked/index/untracked nonignored state is dirty, and post-lock validation must require that the derived lock commit changes only audit-lock.json.
reproduction.observed: Both creator and post-lock validator accepted the unreviewed staged path in the lock commit.

findings.impact: The reviewed baseline is no longer the complete reviewed state immediately preceding audit execution: unreviewed policy, documentation, implementation, or other nonlocked bytes can enter the authoritative lock commit and become ancestors of every later lane seal without invalidating the lock. This defeats the claimed clean-baseline/direct-child provenance boundary and makes lock-commit scope depend on operator discipline rather than a replayable invariant.
findings.recommendation: Before doing any creator work, require a clean index and clean nonignored worktree (for example, parse git status --porcelain=v2 --untracked-files=all and reject every entry). In validate_lock, derive the lock commit and require its full diff-tree path set to equal only docs/qa/implementation-readiness/correctness-audit/audit-lock.json. Add temporary-Git controls for unstaged, staged, and untracked nonignored pre-creator state and for an otherwise valid direct-child lock commit containing a second path; require both creator and post-lock validator to reject.

findings.title: The authoritative status still says candidate 5 is pending in a dirty canonical worktree
findings.claim: PROJECT_STATUS.md is the declared current-state authority, but its Resume Checkpoint says candidate 4's fix is in the dirty canonical worktree pending candidate 5. In the same file, later bullets say candidate 5 exists, validates green, and is awaiting review. Live Git evidence shows the canonical source checkout and review checkout are both clean at candidate 5. The contradictory committed-vs-dirty statement was not caught by validate_project_status.py.

evidence.detail: Line 23 says the fix is in the dirty canonical worktree pending candidate 5, while lines 27-29 describe candidate 5 as present, validated, and awaiting baseline review.
The status validator checks required phrases, counts, and linked paths but has no consistency assertion for candidate number, committed HEAD, or clean/dirty state.

evidence.gitEvidence: Under a separately acquired nonblocking canonical workspace flock, /home/smithers/projects/nemesis-card-corpus/repos/nemesis-retaliation reported branch work/card-corpus-extraction, HEAD d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec, tree e148ed6db227256b15c1d4ba79c2ebcb1171d4bd, and no status entries. The assigned branch reported the same HEAD/tree and no status entries.

findings.reproduction: Read PROJECT_STATUS.md:23 at candidate HEAD, then compare git status --porcelain=v2 and git rev-parse HEAD in the canonical source and assigned review worktrees. The text says dirty/pending candidate 5; both repositories are clean at candidate 5.
findings.impact: A fresh-session integrator following the declared status authority receives mutually inconsistent provenance state and could incorrectly treat committed candidate-5 bytes as uncommitted or resume candidate creation instead of review/disposition. It also weakens the audit trail for the committed-vs-dirty boundary under review.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the stale bullet as explicitly historical and state that candidate 5 is committed and clean at d78e91e9f0d29eab7e9d838d4fc043ba73518cec. Add a bounded status check that the named active candidate/branch state does not simultaneously contain 'dirty ... pending candidate 5' and 'candidate 5' current-state claims.

requiredBeforePromotion: introduce audit-lock.json in the baseline's immediate direct-child commit before any lane begins

activeAuditLockSupersession.note: No actual active lock is being silently superseded in candidate 5. The separate finding concerns future direct-child lock-commit scope, not the disposition of the preserved v1 lock.
